title: ANDS Studio — Dossier catalog / workspace home
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top navigation bar. On the left, a dot and "ANDS Studio · dossier manager"; across it, icon-and-label chips link to "Journey", "Dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Help", with the active one highlighted. A user chip sits at the far right.

Below, the heading "Your product dossiers" appears beside a "Grid / List" view toggle, a "View archived (trash)" button, and a "New dossier +" button. An explanatory paragraph states that a Dossier ID "is the permanent file for one product at Health Canada", that opening a dossier lets you build its eCTD Module 1–5, and that client workspaces are isolated end-to-end. Several terms (Dossier ID, eCTD, Module 1) carry glossary tooltips.

If you have no dossiers, a notice says "No dossiers yet. Create one to start building a submission." (While the list fetches you briefly see "Loading dossiers…".)

Clicking "New dossier +" (button toggles to "Cancel") opens an inline card. It has "Dossier ID" (placeholder "e123456", with format help), "Product name" (placeholder "Drugazole 10 mg tablet"), a "Submission type" dropdown (ANDS, SANDS, SNDS), and optional "Client / sponsor" and "Owner (PM)" fields. Choosing ANDS reveals a "Comparative-BE only (CS-BE path…)" checkbox. Small print explains that Health Canada issues your Dossier ID via a Dossier ID Request through REP (via your CESG account); a link-style "No ID yet? Start with a placeholder →" auto-fills a generated ID starting with "d" plus six digits. You press "Create & open →" (shows "Creating…"). An invalid ID shows a red notice: "Dossier ID must be one letter + 6–7 digits (e.g. e123456)". On success a toast confirms creation and you go into the dossier's Module 1 workspace.

Once dossiers exist, a triage bar offers a filter input ("Filter by product, ID, type, client or owner…"), a "Just my dossiers" checkbox, and an "N of N" count. In Grid view each dossier is a clickable tile: its ID, product title, a meta line (submission type, and CS-BE when applicable, plus sponsor), a progress bar, and a status chip ("Ready to file" or "N/N modules"). Placeholder dossiers carry a "draft ID — set real ✎" chip; each tile has a "✕" delete button. List view shows a sortable table with Dossier ID, Product, Status, Type, Client / sponsor, Owner, and Soonest due (overdue dates flagged).

Clicking delete opens a modal, "Delete this dossier?", explaining the dossier is archived rather than destroyed and recorded on the audit trail; you type the Dossier ID and enter a required reason before "Archive dossier" enables. The rename chip opens "Set the real Health Canada Dossier ID", where you enter a new ID and an optional reason, then press "Apply new ID". "View archived (trash)" reveals an "Archived (recoverable)" list showing when and by whom each was archived, with a "Restore ↩" button. Delete and restore raise confirming toasts.
